question: Three bags contain balls as follows: Bag I has 2 white, 4 black; Bag II has 3 white, 5 black; Bag III has 4 white, 2 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball is drawn from it. (a) What is the probability that the ball drawn is white? (b) If the ball drawn is white, what is the probability it was drawn from Bag III? (c) If two balls are drawn successively (with replacement of the first) from the same bag, what is the probability both are white?
explanation:
Let E1: Bag I, E2: Bag II, E3: Bag III is chosen. Each bag is equally likely.
Thus, $P(E_1) = P(E_2) = P(E_3) = \dfrac{1}{3}$
Let W: Ball drawn is white.

$P(W|E_1) = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$P(W|E_2) = \dfrac{3}{8}$
$P(W|E_3) = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

(a)
$P(W) = \sum_{i=1}^{3} P(E_i)P(W|E_i)$
$= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3}$
$= \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{2}{9}$
First, $\dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{3}{9} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
So,
$P(W) = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{8+3}{24} = \dfrac{11}{24}$

(b) By Bayes' theorem:
$P(E_3|W) = \frac{P(E_3)P(W|E_3)}{P(W)}$
$= \frac{\dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3}}{\dfrac{11}{24}}$
$= \frac{\dfrac{2}{9}}{\dfrac{11}{24}} = \frac{2}{9} \times \frac{24}{11} = \frac{48}{99}$

(c) Probability that both draws are white (chosen bag is not known):
Total probability:
$= \sum_{i=1}^{3} P(E_i) [P(W|E_i)]^2$
$= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \left(\dfrac{3}{8}\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2$
$= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{9}{64} + \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{4}{9}$
$= \dfrac{1}{27} + \dfrac{9}{192} + \dfrac{4}{27}$
Now, $\dfrac{1}{27} + \dfrac{4}{27} = \dfrac{5}{27}$
$\dfrac{9}{192} = \dfrac{3}{64}$
Total = $\dfrac{5}{27} + \dfrac{3}{64}$
Take LCM = 1728
$\dfrac{5 \times 64}{1728} + \dfrac{3 \times 27}{1728}$
$= \dfrac{320 + 81}{1728} = \dfrac{401}{1728}$

Final Answers:
(a) $\dfrac{11}{24}$
(b) $\dfrac{48}{99}$
(c) $\dfrac{401}{1728}$
